messages:
Maya: Hey all, hi I'm Maya — just started today. Got an M1 Air and trying to get a consistent dev stack set up. Primary targets: python (3.10/3.11), node, and a small go tool. Following the handbook but running into a couple of snags: brew installs but `brew` not found until I restart terminal, asdf node plugin complains about missing gpg keys, and direnv keeps asking to allow before it loads env vars. Any recommended minimal dotfiles changes?

Tomas: welcome Maya! For brew on Apple Silicon you should add this to ~/.zprofile (or ~/.profile if you use bash):

```
# Homebrew
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
```

That avoids needing a full restart.

Maya: ah ok that fixed the brew visibility. Still seeing `ERROR: gpg keys missing` when installing node with asdf.

InfraBot: Nodejs plugin requires importing the release GPG keys used for nodejs releases. Quick steps:
1) Install gpg: `brew install gnupg`
2) Run plugin's provided import: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`
If that fails behind corp VPN, set `GPG_TTY=$(tty)` before running.

Riley: For direnv, make sure you run `direnv allow` inside the repo root after adding `.envrc`. If you want auto-allow for personal projects, consider `direnv edit .` to create a minimal `.envrc` that sources `~/.envs/shared` and then `direnv allow` once. We recommend never checking secrets into git — add `.envrc` to .gitignore but keep `.envrc.example` in the repo.

Maya: thanks! One more: asdf python install fails with `C compiler is required`. Should I install xcode CLI tools?

Tomas: yep, run `xcode-select --install`. Also brew install `openssl@1.1` and `readline` if you get SSL or readline build errors, then set env when building: `export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"` before `asdf install python 3.11.4`. Or prefer installing python via `brew install python@3.11` if you don't need per-project versions.

Nina: fyi if you want to keep dotfiles minimal, I use a tiny set: `.zprofile` with brew+asdf init; `.zshrc` with aliases and `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"`; `~/.gitconfig` with name/email and `~/.ssh/config` with jump host entries. Example ssh config we use internally:

```
Host jump
  HostName jump.prod.redwood.com
  User nina

Host internal-*
  ProxyJump jump
  ForwardAgent yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood
```

That way you can `ssh internal-db01` without long flags.

Maya: nice. Is it OK to store `NO_PROXY` and registry vars in ~/.envs/shared and use direnv to load it? Concerned about leaking to dotfiles repo.

InfraBot: yes store sensitive envs in a local-only file. Our recommended pattern: `~/.envs/shared` with `export NO_PROXY=...` and then in repo `.envrc` add `source_env ~/.envs/shared` (direnv supports that). Make sure `~/.envs` is in your .gitignore and never committed.

Maya: super helpful. I'll update my dotfiles and ping infra if I hit more fails. I'll also drop a short checklist in #new-hires once it's tidy. Thanks all! :heart:
